31751-what-bird-is-that.title: According To Season
31751-what-bird-is-that.creator: Frank M. Chapman
31751-what-bird-is-that.description: A book by Frank M. Chapman. BEFORE a leaf unfolds or a flower spreads its petals, even before the buds swell, and while yet there is snow on the ground, the birds tell us that spring is at hand. The Song Sparrow sings "Spring, spring, spring, sunny days are here"; the Meadowlark blows his fife, the Downy rattles his drum, and company after company of Grackles in glistening black coats, and of Red-wings with scarlet epaulets, go trooping by.

arxiv-2001-05058.title: Hippocampus Segmentation on Epilepsy and Alzheimer’s Disease Studies with Multiple Convolutional Neural Networks Journal: Helyion Source code: https://github.com/MICLab-Unicamp/e2dhipseg , published in Heliyon https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405844021003315 (DOI: 10.1016/j.heliyo
arxiv-2001-05058.creator: Diedre Carmo, Bruna Silva, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, Clarissa Yasuda, Letícia Rittner, Roberto Lotufo
arxiv-2001-05058.description: Abstract Background: Hippocampus segmentation on magnetic resonance imaging is of key importance for the diagnosis, treatment decision and investigation of neuropsychiatric disorders. Automatic segmentation is an active research field, with many recent models using deep learning. Most current state-of-the art hippocampus segmentation methods train their methods on healthy or Alzheimer’s disease patients from public datasets.

arxiv-2201-12575.title: Giant atoms with time-dependent couplings
arxiv-2201-12575.creator: Lei Du, Yao-Tong Chen, Yan Zhang, Yong Li
arxiv-2201-12575.description: Abstract We study the decay dynamics of a two-level giant atom that is coupled to a waveguide with time-dependent coupling strengths. In the non-Markovian regime where the retardation effect cannot be ignored, we show that the dynamics of the atom depends on the atom-waveguide coupling strengths at an earlier time.

arxiv-2204-03190.title: Universal Treatment of Reduction for One-Loop Integrals in Projective Space
arxiv-2204-03190.creator: Bo Feng, Jianyu Gong, Tingfei Li
arxiv-2204-03190.description: Abstract Recently a nice work about the understanding of one-loop integrals has been done in Arkani-Hamed:2017ahv using the tricks of the projective space language associated to their Feynman parametrization. We find this language is also very suitable to deal with the reduction problem of one-loop integrals with general tensor structures as well as propagators with arbitrary higher powers.

arxiv-2301-08704.description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigate the poset 𝐎𝐅 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{OF}(X) of free open filters on a given space X X . In particular, we characterize spaces for which 𝐎𝐅 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{OF}(X) is a lattice.

arxiv-2306-08992.title: On a kinematic proof of Andoyer variables canonicity
arxiv-2306-08992.creator: Anatoly Neishtadt
arxiv-2306-08992.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Anatoly Neishtadt. We present a kinematic proof that the Andoyer variables in rigid body dynamics are canonical. This proof is based on the approach of “virtual rotations” by H. The difference from the original proof by Andoyer is that we do not assume that the fixed in body frame is the frame of principal moments of inertia, and do not use explicit formulas for the kinetic energy of the body that include moments of inertia.

arxiv-2402-13803.title: Collapse of inelastic hard spheres in dimension d ≥ 2 d\geq 2
arxiv-2402-13803.creator: Théophile Dolmaire, Juan J. L. Velázquez
arxiv-2402-13803.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Théophile Dolmaire, Juan J. L. Velázquez. We investigate the collapse of three inelastic particles in dimension d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . We obtain general results of convergence and asymptotics concerning the variables of the dynamical system describing a collapsing system of particles. We prove a complete classification of the singularities when a collapse of three particles takes place, obtaining only two possible orders of collisions between the particles.

arxiv-2412-19969.title: Superconducting Diode Effect in Double Quantum Dot Device
arxiv-2412-19969.creator: Go Takeuchi and Mikio Eto
arxiv-2412-19969.description: Abstract Superconducting diode effect (SDE) is theoretically examined in double quantum dot coupled to three superconducting leads, L L , R ​ 1 R1 and R ​ 2 R2 . Lead L L is commonly connected to two quantum dots (QD1, QD2) while lead R ​ 1 R1 ( R ​ 2 R2 ) is connected to QD1 (QD2) only.

arxiv-2509-25369.title: Generative Value Conflicts Reveal LLM Priorities
arxiv-2509-25369.creator: Andy Liu Kshitish Ghate Mona Diab Daniel Fried Atoosa Kasirzadeh Max Kleiman-Weiner
arxiv-2509-25369.description: Abstract Past work seeks to align large language model (LLM)-based assistants with a target set of values, but such assistants are frequently forced to make tradeoffs between values when deployed. In response to the scarcity of value conflict in existing alignment datasets, we introduce ConflictScope , an automatic pipeline to evaluate how LLMs prioritize different values.

arxiv-2602-12806.title: RAT-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Text Anonymization
arxiv-2602-12806.description: Abstract Data containing personal information is increasingly used to train, fine-tune, or query Large Language Models (LLMs). Text is typically scrubbed of identifying information prior to use, often with tools such as Microsoft’s Presidio or Anthropic’s PII purifier. pmc-10516557.title: Basic CSF parameters and MRZ reaction help in differentiating MOG antibody-associated autoimmune disease versus multiple sclerosis
pmc-10516557.creator: Benjamin Vlad, Ina Reichen, Stephan Neidhart, Marc Hilty, Dimitra Lekaditi, Christine Heuer, Amanda Eisele, Mario Ziegler, Markus Reindl, Andreas Lutterotti, Axel Regeniter, Ilijas Jelcic
pmc-10516557.description: BackgroundMyelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated autoimmune disease (MOGAD) is a rare monophasic or relapsing inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system (CNS) and can mimic multiple sclerosis (MS). The variable availability of live cell-based MOG-antibody assays and difficulties in interpreting low-positive antibody titers can complicate diagnosis.

pmc-11352587.title: Neural Substrates for Early Data Reduction in Fast Vision: A Psychophysical Investigation
pmc-11352587.creator: Serena Castellotti, Maria Michela Del Viva
pmc-11352587.description: To ensure survival, the visual system must rapidly extract the most important elements from a large stream of information. This necessity clashes with the computational limitations of the human brain, so a strong early data reduction is required to efficiently process information in fast vision.

pmc-11446918.title: The biogeography of the Amazonian tree flora
pmc-11446918.creator: Bruno Garcia Luize, Hanna Tuomisto, Robin Ekelschot, Kyle G. Dexter, Iêda L. do Amaral, Luiz de Souza Coelho, Francisca Dionízia de Almeida Matos, Diógenes de Andrade Lima Filho, Rafael P. Salomão, Florian Wittmann, Carolina V. Castilho, Marcelo de Jesus Veiga Carim, Juan Ernesto Guevara, Oliver L.
pmc-11446918.description: We describe the geographical variation in tree species composition across Amazonian forests and show how environmental conditions are associated with species turnover. Our analyses are based on 2023 forest inventory plots (1 ha) that provide abundance data for a total of 5188 tree species. Within-plot species composition reflected both local environmental conditions (especially soil nutrients and hydrology) and geographical regions.

pmc-11518473.title: Overcoming barriers in implementing healthy school nutrition policies: insights from Ukraine
pmc-11518473.creator: T Yurochko, L Heiko
pmc-11518473.description: The general mortality rate from NCDs in Ukraine exceeds that in European Union countries, (Yurochko et al., 2023) exacerbated by the ongoing war. Healthy nutrition plays a pivotal role in enhancing the overall quality of life and curbing the prevalence of non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

pmc-11684738.title: Comparative Assessment of Water Models in Protein–Glycan Interaction: Insights from Alchemical Free Energy Calculations and Molecular Dynamics Simulations
pmc-11684738.creator: Deng Li, Mona S Minkara
pmc-11684738.description: Accurate computational simulations of protein–glycan dynamics are crucial for a comprehensive understanding of critical biological mechanisms, including host–pathogen interactions, immune system defenses, and intercellular communication. The accuracy of these simulations, including molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and alchemical free energy calculations, critically relies on the appropriate parameters, including the water model, because of the extensive hydrogen bonding with glycan hydroxyl groups.

pmc-11709860.title: Effects of menopause in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease and comorbid metabolic disease
pmc-11709860.creator: Charly Abi‐Ghanem, Abigail E Salinero, Richard D Kelly, Krystyna A Rybka, Olivia J Gannon, Kasey M Belanger‐Mayer, Christina A Thrasher, Emily Groom, Rachel Smith, Heddwen L Brooks, Damian G Zuloaga, Kristen L Zuloaga
pmc-11709860.description: BackgroundAbout two‐thirds of those with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are women, most of whom are post‐menopausal. Menopause accelerates the risk for dementia by increasing the risk for metabolic, cardiovascular, and cerebrovascular diseases. Mid‐life metabolic disease (e.g. obesity, diabetes, or prediabetes) is a well‐known risk factor for dementia.

pmc-12534968.title: Surviving against the odds: a qualitative exploration of the resilience of adults experiencing homelessness in Accra, Ghana
pmc-12534968.creator: Benedict Osei Asibey, Brahmaputra Marjadi, Elizabeth Conroy
pmc-12534968.description: BackgroundMost research on the homeless population has focused on the negative attributes and adversities they face. While these are important issues for research, focusing on them alone through a deficit lens may further advance the belief that such people have little or no capacities and skills for survival.

pmc-13169677.title: Association between triglyceride-glucose index and branch retinal vein occlusion: linking metabolic risk to ocular vascular disease
pmc-13169677.creator: Caner Öztürk, Sabriye Bolat, Mustafa Duran, Selim Cevher
pmc-13169677.description: BackgroundTo investigate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO), and to evaluate its diagnostic performance.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, 49 patients with newly diagnosed BRVO and 50 age- and sex-matched controls were enrolled. All participants underwent a complete ophthalmic examination, and venous blood samples were collected after overnight fasting.

pmc-13202262.title: Characterization of antioxidant qualities and exploration of mechanisms in different colored onions: Insights from metabolomics and systems biology
pmc-13202262.creator: Chenglong He, Johane Johari Mkunga, Dongsheng Zhang, Muhammad Iqbal Choudhary, Wenxi Zhai, Xinrong Xie, Liyue Fei, Chunhui Shan, Xinquan Yang, Wenchao Cai
pmc-13202262.description: Onion color correlates with nutritional value, however, systematic studies assessing antioxidant properties across different colored varieties remain limited. This research integrates chemometrics, metabolomics, and systems biology to evaluate antioxidant quality and underlying mechanisms. Purple onions exhibited the highest total phenolic and flavonoid content, along with superior water-soluble free radical scavenging and reduction capacity.

pmc-13338596.title: Rh(III)-catalyzed chelation-assisted C–H activation/annulation of 2-arylimidazolines with cyclic diazo-1,3-dicarbonyl compounds: a novel approach to tetracyclic annulated derivatives of 2,3-dihydroimidazo[2,1-a]isoquinoline
pmc-13338596.creator: Ivan Lyutin, Grigory Kantin, Olga Bakulina, Dmitry Dar'in, Ilan Marek
pmc-13338596.description: 2-Arylimidazolines were annulated with cyclic diazo-1,3-dicarbonyl compounds under Rh(III)-catalysis for the first time. The developed general and efficient approach based on CH-activation allowed the efficient preparation of five novel types of tetraheterocyclic systems derived from 2,3-dihydroimidazo[2,1-a]isoquinolines fused with an additional five-, six- or seven-membered carbocycle or N-/O-heterocycle.

pmc-13491985.title: Development and validation of the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) questionnaire on pediatric pain management for physicians and nurses
pmc-13491985.creator: Qiao Shen, Xiaoqiong Wei, Wei Liu, Wenni Zhang, Hongyao Leng, Xianlan Zheng
pmc-13491985.description: BackgroundEffective pediatric pain management is often hindered by gaps in medical staff’s knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Few reliable instruments comprehensively measure these domains. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate a Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) Questionnaire on pediatric pain management for physicians and nurses.

pmc-13511182.title: Inflammation Meets Ventricular Dynamics: Combined Hematologic and Radiologic Predictors of Shunt-Dependent Hydrocephalus in Endovascularly Treated Patients with Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
pmc-13511182.creator: Ali Arslan, Zeki Boga, Semih Kivanc Olguner, Zişan Nur Sürmelioğlu, Mustafa Emre Sarac, Mehmet Ozer, Ali Harmanoğullarından, Ali Sürmelioğlu, Vedat Acik, Yurdal Gezercan
pmc-13511182.description: Background/Objectives: Shunt-dependent hydrocephalus remains a major complication following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Although several clinical–radiological prediction models have been proposed, the additional contribution of inflammatory biomarkers remains unclear. This study evaluated whether the platelet-to-neutrophil ratio provides additional predictive value beyond established clinical and radiological predictors of shunt-dependent hydrocephalus after aSAH.

pmc-13549666.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practices regarding climate change and its oral health effects among dental health care providers in India. A cross-sectional study
pmc-13549666.creator: M Vaishno Preethi, K Priya Deepa Lakshmi, M Muthu Sruthi, M Hemagayathri, Devi S Brinda, V Subhalakshmi
pmc-13549666.description: Background: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a major public health threat. Despite its growing relevance, the implications for oral health and the preparedness of future dental professionals remain underexplored. This study assessed dental students' knowledge, attitude, and practices (KAP) regarding climate change and its effects on oral health.
